title: The Righteous Wazir Wrongfully Gaoled

full_text:
In the Persian city of Shiraz served a righteous Grand Vizier named Nizam al-Mulk, who was beloved by the people for his incorruptible justice.
Corrupt courtiers, unable to bribe him, forged letters implying that the Vizier was plotting with foreign powers. Deceived by these forged scrolls, the young Sultan stripped Nizam of his offices and cast him into the darkest subterranean dungeon of the citadel.

Months passed. The dungeon warden, expecting to find the former Vizier weeping in misery or offering bribes for release, was amazed to find Nizam sitting calmly on his stone bench, carving chess pieces from fallen limestone and composing verses of spiritual contentment.

The warden asked: 'Master, how canst thou remain serene in this damp darkness after ruling an empire?'
Nizam replied with a calm smile:
'I possess four medicines that cure all despair:
First: The certainty that nothing occurs without divine decree.
Second: The knowledge that impatience only multiplies suffering.
Third: The awareness that whatever happens could have been worse.
Fourth: The clear conscience that I never wronged an innocent soul or took a dishonest copper.
Stone walls can bind my limbs, but they cannot imprison an innocent heart.'

Meanwhile, without Nizam's wise guidance, the kingdom fell into chaos: tax collectors embezzled revenues, banditry flourished on trade routes, and the treasury emptied.
The Sultan, realizing something was deeply wrong, re-examined the forged documents and discovered the watermark of the corrupt chamberlain!

Overcome with remorse, the Sultan rushed down to the dungeon in person, fell to his knees before Nizam, and wept:
'O wise father, forgive my reckless blindness! Return to the diwan and govern our realm!'

Nizam gently raised the young king, harbored no resentment, and returned to his duties. The corrupt chamberlain was banished, and the Sultan learned never again to condemn a faithful servant without indisputable proof.
moral: Patience, clear conscience, and unwavering integrity endure through prison walls until truth prevails.
